subject: Pricing exhibit: proposed "Usage Buffer Escrow" and suspension protocol
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Fisher <tom.fisher@acme-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibit: Usage buffer / escrow proposal

Laura — thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and we have one ask tied to short-term usage volatility during onboarding and predictable unit economics.

Summary of Acme's proposal (attached: ACME_marked_pricing_exhibit_v2.pdf):
- Add a "Usage Buffer Escrow": buyer pays an upfront escrow equal to 8% of the first 12 months' committed spend to cover transient overages during the first 90 days post-go-live.
- Escrow release: 50% released after 90 days if usage stays within 110% of forecast, remaining 50% released after 180 days subject to reconciliation/true-up.
- Suspension carveout: if usage exceeds 150% of forecast for any 14-day window, buyer can request a temporary suspension of overage billing while we run remediation for up to 14 days.

Our commercial team prefers an escrow vs. a permanent surcharge so we can avoid ongoing price floors. Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to accept an escrow structure and whether you can live with the release schedule? We need legal redlines by EOD Wednesday 25th to keep our internal board timeline.

Best,
Emily Stone
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

-----

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: Usage buffer / escrow proposal

Emily — thanks for the clear proposal and the markup. We appreciate the preference for a temporary escrow mechanism; that's a constructive alternative to an ongoing surcharge.

High-level reaction from commercial: we can accept an escrow approach but propose the following compromises to keep unit economics predictable for both parties:
- Buffer size: agree to a time-limited buffer but suggest 5% of 12-month committed spend (not 8%) as a midpoint for the first go-live period.
- Release cadence: align on a 90-day initial release of 40% and an 180-day final release after reconciliation (we prefer earlier partial release to avoid cash pressure on Acme).
- Trigger thresholds: we want a clear definition of "usage" metric (billable tokens or API calls) and an explicit reconciliation formula; propose a bilateral audit right limited to one review during the 180-day window.
- Suspension: we can offer a temporary suspension window (up to 7 days, not 14) for remediation; longer suspensions would require explicit executive approval and service credits in lieu of suspension.

Rishi / Karthik — can you weigh in on the legal wording we should propose for a "Usage Buffer Escrow" section in the pricing exhibit? Ben, can you draft the alternate exhibit that implements the 5%/40%-60% release cadence?

Emily — we can turn around a redline by COB Thursday (26th) if Legal confirms the structure below. If Acme can accept the 5% buffer + 40/60 release schedule and the 7-day suspension cap, I think we're close.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales — Enterprise

Laura / team — quick legal notes to support the commercial ask. Attached is a marked-up doc we can translate into the pricing exhibit. Key points below: 

1) Definitions: add explicit definitions for "Usage Buffer", "Release Event", "Reconciliation Period", and the unit of measurement ("Billable Units" = API calls or token-equivalents as defined in Exhibit A).
2) Escrow mechanism: prefer an escrow (third-party custodian) to be named in the exhibit; escrow should be returned to Buyer if Redwood materially breaches or if final reconciliation shows no overages.
3) Release mechanics: define a "Release Event" — e.g., 40% released on Day 90 if cumulative usage <= 110% of forecast; remainder released on Day 180 after mutual reconciliation and any agreed offsets.
4) Suspension language: limit automatic suspension to 7 days (as Laura proposed). For anything beyond that, require written executive sign-off and provide a service credit schedule (credits accrue at pro rata daily rates).
5) Liability cap: do NOT create a new unlimited warranty or price floor. Any escrow should expressly not be treated as a pre-payment of future minimums — include language that escrow is for mitigation only and not a price guarantee.
6) Audit & records: limit audits to a single reconciliation review unless material discrepancy (>5%) is found; recoverable audit costs offset to prevailing party.

Attachment: pricing_exhibit_redline_rishi.docx (Word, 48 KB)

If commercial is comfortable with 5% buffer and the 40/60 release cadence, Legal can produce final exhibit language for signature.

- Rishi
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: Usage buffer / escrow proposal — Acme comments

Laura / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few counterpoints from Acme legal: 

- Buffer amount: we can accept 5% if Redwood agrees to extend the escrow release tail to 210 days (i.e., final release no earlier than Day 210) to allow for quarter-end reconciliations. This is critical for our finance close.
- Suspension: 7-day automatic suspension is short for our onboarding workflows; propose 14 days but with a requirement to provide a remediation plan within 72 hours and a cap on the number of suspensions (one per 12-month period).
- Third-party escrow: Acme prefers escrow held in our corporate trust account or via DocuSign/third-party that both sides accept; Tom attached specific language.
- Audit: okay to limit to 1 reconciliation, but Acme wants carveout for fraud or repeated breaches.

We attached ACME_legal_comments.docx with inline edits. If Redwood accepts 5% + 210-day final release + 14-day suspension (with remediation plan and one-suspension cap), we can greenlight procurement. Otherwise we will push for 8% with shorter release.

Tom Fisher
Deputy General Counsel — Commercial Transactions
Acme Corp
